response.justification: The candidate is an experienced generalist software engineer (15+ years) with strong web, backend, and full-stack credentials, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of this Principal Performance Architect role. There is no evidence of SoC/IP modeling, hardware-software co-design, AI accelerator or GPU architecture work, SIMD/MIMD experience, or deep neural network training/inference optimization. The closest adjacent experience is low-latency service work in D at Sociomantic and some C/C++ component work at National Instruments, plus generic 'embedded systems' mention — none of which approaches silicon-level performance architecture. Education is a BS in Computer Science (meets the 8+ years path formally), but the domain expertise gap is too large to bridge at principal level.
strengths: 15+ years of broad software engineering experience, including staff/senior roles
Demonstrated low-latency, high-throughput systems work (millions of req/sec, async I/O, caching)
Some systems-level C/C++ exposure at National Instruments and strong open-source/tooling track record
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, hardware-software co-design, or silicon architecture experience
No AI accelerator, GPU architecture, or deep-learning workload optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack (TypeScript, Node, React), not hardware performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture expertise
No AI accelerator / DNN workload optimization experience
Extensive senior-level software engineering and low-latency systems experience
